oneLiner: Film prediction pools where GenLayer validators verify frozen rules and published box-office results. Stake StudioNet GEN and share the winning pot.
description: Bullseye is a film prediction platform. Choose an opening-weekend revenue range, stake 2–100 StudioNet GEN, and collect your share of the winning pool. Five upcoming films close before previews; Barbie, Oppenheimer and Dune: Part Two offer historical practice with known results. GenLayer validators independently verify frozen rules and read The Numbers for the exact US/Canada result. Pools consume the finalized oracle outcome; no administrator sets a winner. Winners share the whole pot; missing evidence or an empty winning range permits refunds. Claims are nonce-bound and marked paid only after independent exact native-credit verification and finality. Confirmed failed transfers permit a safe retry; pending or ambiguous receipts stay locked. The repo includes adversarial tests, two live payout proofs, exact balances and a tutorial. GEN is simulated StudioNet currency. Open pages drive settlement; the daily keeper awaits authentication. Legacy deployments and proof limits are disclosed.

howTo.heading: Browse upcoming markets
howTo.instruction: Open the website. Upcoming lists five films with fixed ranges and pre-release cutoffs. Select a Street Fighter range to open its 2 GEN ticket. Expand Market rules & result to inspect the source and timing; no wallet is needed to browse.

howTo.heading: Try an instant result
howTo.instruction: Choose Practice, open Barbie, and expand Play for free points. Select $150m – under $200m and confirm without an exact guess. You should see $162,022,044 and 100 practice points. Reload to check persistence. This does not stake GEN.

howTo.heading: Verify GenLayer execution
howTo.instruction: Open docs/CLAIM-RECOVERY.md and its raw receipts. Run npx tsx scripts/verify-claim-recovery.ts for read-only source, native-credit, finality and balance checks. Run the adversarial contract suite and scripts/claim-recovery-ui-check.ts for controlled failure, retry, replay and account-isolation tests. The forecast live payout uses a separate test oracle; no upcoming film is prematurely resolved.

howTo.heading: Optional funded practice
howTo.instruction: Use your own MetaMask/GenLayer-plugin wallet on StudioNet 61999 with at least 2 GEN. Choose Barbie’s $150m – under $200m range in the main GEN ticket, stake 2 GEN and sign. Leave the app open until the shared two-minute session settles; Collect and sign once. GEN received requires an exact credited transfer. Upcoming stakes remain held until their future result or void.

expectedOutcome: Eight GEN markets; five upcoming outcomes remain unknown. Barbie free practice returns $162,022,044 and 100 points. Recovery evidence shows 121 passing contract tests, controlled failed-transfer retries, exact final balances, and successful StudioNet native payouts for both pool implementations. The forecast payout uses an isolated test oracle. New claims become paid only after independent receipt verification; terminal failure opens one retry. No live hosted failed-transfer proof is claimed.
stewardResponse: Both pool contracts reserve nonce-bound claims and record paid only after independent exact native-credit verification and a protected finality callback. Terminal failure permits one next attempt; pending/unknown receipts stay locked. Replays and duplicate claims cannot emit again. Retry requires backing for all unpaid obligations. The app verifies automatically and offers Retry collection after failure finality. 121 contract tests (44 recovery cases), 24 app tests and mobile failure/retry checks pass. Two 2 GEN stakes and actual StudioNet payouts returned the wallet exactly to 8.000999999999999998 GEN; both escrows ended at zero. Failure tests use controlled fixtures; the forecast payout uses an isolated test oracle, leaving listed future outcomes unknown. New contracts and raw source/receipt/balance evidence: https://github.com/JWattjr/Bullseye/blob/main/docs/CLAIM-RECOVERY.md. Legacy contracts are immutable; no retroactive recovery is claimed.
